summary.headline: Orient Cables H1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 103% YoY to ₹1,018 crore, with PAT up 194% to ₹73.7 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported its highest-ever Q2 and H1 FY27 performance: Q2 revenue ₹528 crore (up 107% YoY) and H1 revenue ₹1,018 crore (up 103%). H1 EBITDA rose 155% to ₹119.2 crore at an 11.7% margin (up 240 bps), and H1 PAT rose 194% to ₹73.7 crore, exceeding FY26 full-year EBITDA and PAT. Management guided H2 FY27 absolute performance broadly in line with H1, with Q3 seasonally soft and Q4 recovery. This was the company's maiden earnings call following its October 2026 listing on BSE and NSE.

financial_highlights.change: Realisation gains cited from certain product lines

financial_highlights.value: ~8% of H1 FY27 revenue; ~₹80 crore in H1 FY27 vs ~₹50 crore in H1 FY26 (as stated)

segments.name: Networking cables and solutions
segments.commentary: Largest business (CAT5E–CAT7, CCTV, coaxial, terminated assemblies); management expects its share of revenue to slightly reduce as other segments grow, while the market grows ~18–19% CAGR.

segments.name: Speciality power and optical fibre cables
segments.commentary: Revenue contribution increased in FY27; management cites good OFC offtake from telcos, corporates and exports; margins said to be slightly lower than networking but with lower manufacturing cost.

segments.name: Wire and cable harnesses / EV charging guns and assemblies (OCL Green Tech, 51% subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Entered in FY26; supplies started in Q2/current quarter to tier-one OEMs; ramp-up in Q3 FY27 with full capacity utilisation targeted by Q4 FY27. Contribution currently insignificant.

segments.name: Allied and passive networking products
segments.commentary: Keystone jacks, patch panels, faceplates, gang boxes, power strips and cords; part of cross-selling strategy. No separate numbers disclosed.

segments.name: eBeam irradiated cables and new products
segments.commentary: eBeam commercial production started in FY27 (initially solar cables), railway certification received; solar junction boxes expected to commence commercial production in Q4 FY27; drone cable described as small but high margin.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 absolute performance expected to be broadly in line with H1 FY27; Q3 seasonally softer, Q4 momentum expected to improve.
Current installed capacity expected to be fully utilised by FY28 per management, given current growth.

New Bihari (Rajasthan) plant on 11 acres: civil construction progressing, completion expected H1 FY28; capacity to come into effect from beginning of FY29 (~₹4,500 crore+ expansion referenced in Q&A).
Blended margins expected to remain in the current range and slightly improve over time, driven by new products and R&D.
Commercial production at the 50:50 JV Codeling Cable Technologies (with Aditya Infotec) expected from Q4 FY27; South India Bangalore plant ramping up.
Plans to add high-voltage and medium-voltage cable manufacturing at the large Vivari plant, targeting solar/renewable segment.
capex_capacity: Total installed capacity ~9.63 lakh km per annum across two Vivari plants and one Bengaluru plant; overall capacity utilisation ~72% as of September 2026.
Bengaluru plant began commercial operations in May 2026 with initial capacity ~1,09,320 km per annum; running at 60%+ utilisation in Q2.
Acquired ~42,530 sq m additional land at Vivari for what management calls its largest single manufacturing facility; construction started.
Bihari (Rajasthan) 11-acre land acquired for new plant; civil work in progress.
Peak revenue potential with current capacity cited at ₹2,800–2,900 crore per year.
IPO proceeds: entire ₹155.5 crore earmarked for debt repayment has been utilised; remaining proceeds for plant and machinery and general corporate purposes. Capex to remain demand-led and calibrated.
demand_pricing: Management attributes ~60% of H1 growth to volume and the remainder to realisation, citing better realisations in certain product lines.
Top-four player in India's networking cables; market share rose from ~16% in FY22 to 22.9% in FY26 (as stated).

Top-10 customers associated for an average of over nine years; sales mainly to telecom operators (e.g., Airtel, Jio named in Q&A), with data centre push via OEM partners and a new vertical being built.
Industry data cited: Indian wires & cables market ~₹1,122 bn (FY26) to ₹2,103 bn (FY31), 13.4% CAGR; networking, OFC and eBeam CAGRs of 18.7%, 17.3% and 37.8% (FY26–FY31).
Middle East conflict noted; management says no material impact on raw material or inventory after corrective actions taken.
Management does not disclose product-level margins or segment-wise realisations.

qa_highlights.question: Volume vs realisation split of the 103% revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: About 60% from volume and the balance from realisation, with better realisation from certain product lines.

qa_highlights.question: Margin differences between speciality power/OFC and networking cables?
qa_highlights.answer: Power cables carry slightly lower margins than networking, but lower manufacturing cost keeps overall impact stable; product-level margin and realisation breakup not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Current capacity utilisation and peak revenue potential, and FY28 capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation was 72% as of September; peak revenue potential ~₹2,800–2,900 crore per year. New plant in FY28 with high/medium voltage cable capability; expansion ₹4,500 crore+ and benefit from beginning FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Sustainability of growth momentum and return ratios?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth attributed to utilisation, volume and demand across verticals; management says ROE and ROCE improved in H1 and expects levels to be sustained; Bangalore reached 60%+ utilisation within months.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue potential from EV charging and new products?
qa_highlights.answer: EV gun and cable assemblies supplied to tier-one OEMs from current quarter; railway certification obtained; solar and HV/MV cables and solar junction boxes are further growth drivers.

qa_highlights.question: Will networking cables remain core as mix shifts?
qa_highlights.answer: Networking market expected to grow ~18–19% CAGR; its revenue share will slightly reduce as speciality power, OFC and new segments grow.

risks_watch: Q3 seasonal softness; H2 guidance flat to H1 implies no sequential growth despite 103% H1 growth.
Sustainability of ~100% growth as base enlarges; growth partly from realisation gains that may not persist.
Limited disclosure: no product-level margins or segment revenue breakup; EV, drone and eBeam contributions currently small.
Ramp-up risk for Bangalore, EV assemblies, solar junction boxes (Q4 FY27) and the Codeling JV (Q4 FY27).
Capacity additions (Bihari, Vivari) only effective from FY29; near-term capacity could constrain growth at ~72% utilisation trend towards full use by FY28.
Raw material and Middle East conflict exposure; management says impact so far manageable.
Transcript quality: several Q&A passages are unclear; figures such as export volume and capex should be verified against the filing.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth momentum and returns, with specific numbers, but guarded on H2 by guiding only to broad consistency with H1. Management declined to give product-level margins and realisation splits, and several answers were brief.
key_quotes: We are pleased to report our highest ever quarterly and half yearly performance in Q2 and H1 FY 27.
Accordingly, we expect our absolute performance in H2 FY 27 to be more or less broadly in line with H1 FY 27.
Our Bangalore plant commenced operation in May 2020 with initial installed capacity of about 109,320 kilometers per annum.

growth.why: Management guides H2 FY27 broadly in line with H1 (H1 revenue ₹1,018 cr, +103%), implying a sharp slowdown in YoY growth, backed by the Bengaluru plant at 60%+ utilisation, EV line full utilisation by Q4 FY27, and a ₹4,500 cr+ Rajasthan plant only from FY29; overall utilisation 72% with current capacity expected fully used by FY28.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: H1 FY27 EBITDA margin 11.7% (up 240 bps YoY) and management expects blended margins to stay in range and slightly improve via new products and R&D, though Q3 is seasonally soft and product-level margins are undisclosed.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Codeling JV and Bengaluru ramp-up, plus Bihari plant civil work due H1 FY28 and Vivari expansion under construction; management expects current capacity fully used by FY28 at 72% utilisation, but new capacity only effective from FY29.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: About 60% of H1 FY27 revenue growth (103% YoY) came from volume, Bengaluru at 60%+ utilisation, and EV assemblies ramp from Q3 FY27, yet management guides H2 FY27 only broadly in line with H1, implying a sharp YoY slowdown.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: A ~₹4,500 crore+ expansion is referenced with Bihari civil work in progress and Vivari 42,530 sq m land under construction, while utilisation is only 72%, so further announcements are likely to be demand-led rather than urgent.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided H2 FY27 only to be broadly in line with H1 (H1 revenue ₹1,018 crore), a flat-sequential stance that leaves little room for a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Growth partly from realisation gains that may not persist, Q3 seasonal softness, and ramp-up risk for Bengaluru, EV assemblies, solar junction boxes and the Codeling JV all due by Q4 FY27.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Solar junction boxes expected to begin commercial production in Q4 FY27, EV gun and cable assemblies ramping from Q3 FY27, and HV/MV cables planned at Vivari, though contributions are currently small.

rows.label: Tier-one OEM EV charging supply ramp
rows.why: OCL Green Tech EV gun and cable assemblies began supplying tier-one OEMs in Q2, with full capacity utilisation targeted by Q4 FY27 though contribution is currently insignificant.

rows.label: Exports growth
rows.why: Exports reportedly rose from ~₹50 crore in H1 FY26 to ~₹80 crore in H1 FY27 (~60%), but the figure needs verification given transcript quality and the export-share disclosure is unclear.

rows.label: Debt repayment completed from IPO
rows.why: The entire ₹155.5 crore IPO proceeds earmarked for debt repayment have been utilised, reducing interest costs going forward.
